In this test, the Company compared the fair value of each reporting unit to its carrying value. ... fair value of its reporting units using a weighting of fair values derived from the income and market approaches.' Goodwill balance $396M (Mar 2024) vs $398M (Dec 2023).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: TDC voluntarily moved to a QUANTITATIVE (vs qualitative) goodwill impairment test for 2023. The trigger for moving from qualitative to quantitative testing is typically that the qualitative analysis can no longer support a conclusion that fair value 'more likely than not' exceeds carrying value. Verify what changed.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Critical Accounting Policies / Goodwill section + Q1 2024 10-Q Goodwill
rfm_tuples.M_value: The 10-K states explicitly: 'For 2023, the Company performed a quantitative impairment test' — this is a disclosed change in testing approach. Result: no impairment charge taken; reporting-unit fair value exceeds carrying value. Goodwill is small relative to enterprise value ($396M vs market cap implied at ~$4B pre-cutoff drawdown, so ~10%), and TDC is a single-segment business so reporting-unit consolidation risk is low. However, the SWITCH from qualitative to quantitative testing in the same year that Cloud ARR guidance was missed and Q4'23 sales cycles 'elongated' is a Mode-B signal: management's own discount-rate / cash-flow assumptions are now closer to the test threshold than in prior years.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically clean (no impairment), but the methodological switch to quantitative testing reveals that the qualitative cushion has thinned. If FY24 Total ARR contraction continues at the Q1'24 -2% pace, a quantitative test in FY24 could plausibly produce an impairment charge. Mode-B finding the framework is designed to catch — the switch IS the leading indicator, not the impairment.

summary: TDC's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-23) and Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-07) document a clean-credit, Big-4-audited business undergoing a material demand-side ARR deceleration: management reaffirmed Public Cloud ARR guidance of 53-57% YoY at Q3'23, missed it at +47.9% in FY23 (admitted as 'elongated sales cycles' in Q4'23), then in Q1'24 Total ARR went negative YoY (-2%) for the first time in the Tier 3 window and Public Cloud ARR decelerated to +35% with a -$3M sequential decline — the leading-edge signal that cloud absorption is saturating as the on-prem ARR pool depletes (Maintenance/upgrade ARR -46% YoY in Q1'24). Mode-B findings: (1) the Q1 2024 10-Q MD&A REMOVED all four forward outlook ranges that were explicit at Q3'23, relocating guidance to the lower-liability press release; (2) the CRO resigned 2024-04-05 with same-day internal replacement and no transition period, 11 weeks after the guidance miss; (3) goodwill testing methodology switched from qualitative to quantitative in 2023, indicating the cushion thinned; (4) Q1'24 buybacks ran at 4.6x operating cash flow while cash dropped $149M. Constraints on bear thesis: PwC unqualified opinion with 17-year tenure, clean ICFR, $163M net debt with single ESG-pricing amendment, no going-concern language, no customer concentration disclosure, no counterparty mirror evidence. Verdict: NEUTRAL leaning SHORT — the demand-deceleration story is real and the claim-evolution signal is high-conviction, but the balance-sheet/audit profile is too clean to land in deep-SHORT tier. Mid-bucket forensic score reflecting the tension.
